edges.description: Reduced WAC adaptor dosage impairs RNF20/40-mediated histone H2B ubiquitination and downstream neuronal transcriptional regulation.
Loss of WAC disrupts one of its established cellular functions in autophagy regulation
Eye abnormalities are reported in most individuals with intragenic WAC loss-of-function variants; the developmental route from WAC dosage to the ocular findings is not established.
Congenital cardiac malformation reported with WAC loss of function; the developmental route from WAC dosage to the septal defect is not established.
Congenital outflow-tract valve malformation reported with WAC loss of function; the developmental route is not established.
Gastrointestinal dysmotility and constipation occur frequently in WAC-related haploinsufficiency via an unestablished enteric or autonomic mechanism.

Neonatal and childhood hypotonia is present in nearly all individuals with intragenic WAC loss-of-function variants; the neuromuscular or central route from WAC dosage to reduced tone is not established.
Sleep problems are reported in a subset of individuals with intragenic WAC loss-of-function variants; no mechanism linking WAC dosage to sleep regulation has been described.
Dysregulated transcriptional programs during brain development impair GABAergic neuronal maturation and circuit function.
WAC loss perturbs inhibitory neuronal development and brain circuitry
Perturbed inhibitory circuitry contributes to seizure and behavioral phenotypes
WAC-related neurodevelopmental dysfunction manifests as delayed developmental milestones.
The same neurodevelopmental circuit disruption contributes to intellectual disability.
Neurobehavioral abnormalities in WAC-related disease include autistic behavior.
GABAergic-neuron perturbation lowers seizure threshold in DeSanto-Shinawi syndrome.
Syndromic WAC haploinsufficiency includes a recognizable craniofacial gestalt.
The same inhibitory-circuit perturbation that lowers seizure threshold is recorded interictally as focal epileptiform discharges on EEG.
Neurobehavioral abnormalities in WAC-related disease include ADHD and behavioral difficulties alongside the autism phenotype.
Cortical-inhibitory and neurobehavioral circuit dysfunction manifests frequently as attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
Neurobehavioral circuit dysregulation manifests frequently as anxiety in older children and adults with WAC-related disorder.
Every deletion in the series spans the 306 kb overlap that contains WAC, so each one also reduces WAC dosage.

Cardiac malformations were reported in six of seven patients with 10p12p11 deletions. Whether WAC or a neighbouring deleted gene is responsible is not settled, so the edge is drawn from the deletion as a whole.

Visual impairment was reported in all seven patients with 10p12p11 deletions. The edge is drawn from the deletion as a whole because the series does not separate WAC from neighbouring genes; intragenic-variant eye findings are carried by the separate Eye abnormalities phenotype.

Infantile hypotonia is the usual explanation for the feeding problems that accompany it in early infancy; GeneReviews reports the two together as nonspecific features at birth without establishing the oral-motor mechanism.

nodes.description: Cardiac malformation was reported in six of seven patients in the series that defined the 10p12p11 deletion syndrome. It is scoped to the deletion subtype: the intragenic-variant series did not report cardiac malformation, and no frequency for the intragenic form has been established, so this phenotype makes no claim about that subtype. Whether the cardiac finding is attributable to WAC dosage or to neighbouring genes lost in the larger deletions is not settled.
